root_idea.summary: The root centers on taking something secretly and out of sight.
root_idea.development: From covert taking, the lexical family extends to theft and the thief, covert listening, gradual or concealed appropriation, and several figurative or specialized uses. The silk term سَرَقٌ is treated as a divergent lexical item.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Canonical Form I Quranic verb for stealing.
Canonical Form VIII Quranic verb in the construction استرق السمع.
Normalized to the singular masculine active-participle citation form سَارِق.
Normalized to the singular feminine active-participle citation form سَارِقَة.

senses.definition: To steal: to take what is not one's due secretly, often by artifice or from a place of custody.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic occurrences include narrative allegations of theft as well as legal and covenant-related contexts. In juridical formulation, the act is further specified as taking an object from a particular place and in a particular measure; these specifications do not replace the core meaning of covert taking.
The Quranic construction is اِسْتَرَقَ السَّمْعَ, meaning to listen covertly or obtain aural information by stealth. This is a distinct covert-listening use, not merely the ordinary act of stealing.

senses.definition: A thief: one who takes what belongs to another clandestinely.
senses.usage_conditions: An active participle of سَرَقَ; the Quran uses both singular and plural forms in narrative and legal contexts.

senses.definition: A female thief: a woman who takes what belongs to another clandestinely.
senses.usage_conditions: Feminine active-participle counterpart of سَارِقٌ in the Quranic legal expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Stealing; the Form II verbal noun is also used for the act of taking secretly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A derived-form usage related to the basic theft meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To listen secretly or eavesdrop.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression using سَرَقَ with السمع; this classical construction is distinct in form from the Quranic اِسْتَرَقَ السَّمْعَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become hoarse, literally as though one's voice had been stolen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative passive expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be robbed of one's honor or reputation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as a figurative expression; the transmitted wording is noted as uncertain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To pass a night pleasantly or enjoyably.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative idiomatic usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the eye to overcome or overpower someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative expression with the eye as the subject.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a thing, to become hidden, unnoticed, or barely perceptible.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive Form I usage, with a different vocalization from the ordinary transitive theft verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the joints to become weak or feeble.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional bodily-state expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To attribute theft to someone or accuse someone of stealing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Lane reports this in connection with an alternate reading at Qur'an 12:81; it is not the canonical QAC Form I analysis of that occurrence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To take an opportunity to look at or listen to someone by stealth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The Form III construction concerns covertly watching or hearing, especially by exploiting another person's inadvertence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To steal gradually, one thing after another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The derived verb emphasizes successive or piecemeal appropriation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To withdraw, recede, or draw back in order to go away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive Form VII usage, especially with عن someone or something.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become languid, weak, or feeble.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate intransitive bodily-state use of the Form VII verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deceive or circumvent secretly or by stealth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative Form VIII usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To suppress or omit some items from an account.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized figurative usage applied to a writer's treatment of accounting entries.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To manure land with dung.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Quadriliteral derived verb formed from the noun سِرْقِينٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A piece or oblong piece of silk; also silk generally.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A textile noun reported as an Arabicized term and divergent from the central covert-taking branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Theft.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A noun derived from or associated with سَرَقَ; vocalized and nominally distinct from the verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thing stolen; by extension, a stolen piece of poetry or verse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Plural usage can refer to appropriated poetic material.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dung used as manure, especially dung of horses and other solid-hoofed animals.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A loanword with variant forms, including سَرْقِينٌ and سَرْجِينٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thievish; a great thief.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An epithet applied to a man or a dog.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stealer of poetry or verses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized agent noun for literary appropriation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Very thievish; a very great thief.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive epithet with no reported plural.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease affecting the limbs or members.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized bodily term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An iron collar or restraint by which the hands are confined together to the neck, attached to fetters or shackles.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is a separate classical noun from the Quranic feminine active participle سَارِقَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The adjuncts or projections in the catches of a lock.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Plural technical usage related to the specialized noun سَارِقَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hoarse in voice; of a young gazelle, having a nasal sound or twang in its cry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative descriptions based on the idea of a voice having been stolen.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Listening by stealth, like a thief.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Active-participle usage associated with covert hearing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Defective or weak in make.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative descriptive usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Weak in speech or expression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized construction with القول.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Short or contracted in the neck.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A bodily descriptive construction.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Covers the basic theft meaning and the derived-form stealing usage.
Idiomatic passing of a night pleasantly.

Form III covert looking and listening.
A stolen thing and appropriated poetic material.

cautions: The Form VIII Quranic occurrence is the specific construction اِسْتَرَقَ السَّمْعَ, meaning covert listening; the contextual English gloss “steals” does not by itself define the sense.
سَارِقَةٌ is the Quranic feminine active participle “female thief,” while Lane also records a separate homonymous classical noun for an iron restraint; these are kept distinct.
The reported Form II reading meaning “was accused of theft” at 12:81 is not the canonical QAC form-group analysis, which records the Form I verb.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: The Lane wording for the figurative expression interpreted as being robbed of one's honor is explicitly treated as a possible mistranscription; it is retained as a qualified Classical Arabic meaning rather than treated as certain standard wording.
